ticket.title: relink reads a key inside a path as a citation, and rewrites superseded event payloads
ticket.description:
Found 2026-11-10 by writing a ticket note, not by a test. Two ways `relink` mistakes one thing for another.  (1) A DEAD KEY INSIDE A PATH IS NOT A REFERENCE. GB-350 documents orphaned blueprints, so its note quotes a few by filename - the old key with an extension. relink cannot tell that from a citation of a ticket, so it proposed rewriting the ticket description and creating THREE LINKS to member tickets that have nothing to do with GB-350. The links are the serious half: a false edge is worse than a stale citation, because it asserts that one ticket carries anothers work. The same shape appears in any prose that names a file: CHANGELOG entries, README examples, commit-style text.  (2) SUPERSEDED EVENT PAYLOADS ARE REWRITTEN. After the served description was corrected, one repair remained: an older task_updated payload of the same ticket still quoted the old filenames. relink rewrites every event payload, but only the LAST one supplies the served value, so that repair changed a description nobody reads - history edited for no effect on state. The remint has the same behaviour and it is wrong there for the same reason.  Suggested shape: rewrite the payload that wins on replay and leave superseded ones alone; and treat a dead key as a reference only when it is not part of a path (a key followed by an extension or sitting inside a path segment is data, not a pointer). Both are testable against a fixture that carries such prose. Until then the operator has to read the dry run, which is exactly the position this session was in.

BOTH HALVES FIXED 2026-11-10 (storypole 123742d).

1. A key inside a path is no longer a citation. `cites_bare` treats a match behind a separator or in front of a file
extension as data, and relink asks it for both the repair decision and the link evidence. The remint still rewrites both,
because it renames the files too; the difference is now an explicit `PlanPath` argument rather than two passes quietly
disagreeing about what a path means.

2. Only the payload that wins on replay is rewritten. Replay keeps the last `task_updated`, so the earlier ones were
history being edited for no effect on state - and their presence kept a corrected ticket reporting work to do.

Tests: a filename is not a citation; a superseded payload is left alone. Both fail against the previous behaviour.

RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden. The filter that decides which keys a ticket cites is per FILE, not per occurrence. If
the same key appears both as a bare citation and inside a path in one ticket, the key stays in the mapping and the rewrite
touches the path occurrence too - so that one case would still corrupt a filename. Nothing in the suite does it today, and
closing it needs the bare-only rule inside the replacement itself rather than at the mapping boundary.

RESIDUAL CLOSED 2026-11-10 — the rule moved into the replacement, so a file filter no longer has to guess.

WHAT WAS LEFT. The bare-only rule was applied at the mapping boundary: a dead key was dropped from a file's mapping when
it appeared only as a path. That was right when every occurrence in a file had the same shape, and wrong when a ticket
both cites a key and names a file containing it - the key stayed in the mapping, and the rewrite then touched the path
too.

WHAT CHANGED. `replace_token` now takes the shape it is replacing under, so the decision is made per occurrence:
  Citations::Anywhere   every whole-token match, paths included - what a remint needs, because it renames the file too
  Citations::Bare       a match inside a path is data and is left alone - what a relink needs, because nothing moves
The two passes are now one named struct rather than separate flags that could be paired wrongly:
  Rewrite::REMINT  = { citations: Anywhere, plan_path: Moves }
  Rewrite::RELINK  = { citations: Bare,     plan_path: Stays }
and each call site says which pass it is instead of threading a lone plan-path argument.

PROVED BY THE CASE THAT WAS BROKEN. `a_path_is_left_alone_even_when_the_same_key_is_cited_bare` builds a description that
does both - "carried by GB-9, blueprint at plans/GB-9.md" - applies relink, and requires the citation to move while the
filename does not. Under the per-file rule the filename became plans/MTR-1.md, so the test fails against the behaviour it
replaced.

SUITE EFFECT: NONE, and that is the point. Re-running relink over the suite still reports nothing to relink; the change
removes a way to be wrong rather than a visible fault.

Also split while here, both for the 250-line rule: `remint/rules.rs` holds the token-level rules and `rewrite.rs` the
document shape they apply to; `relink/citation_tests.rs` holds the tests about which occurrences count.

ALREADY DONE, verified 2026-11-10: the citation rule now applies per occurrence, closed as the residual in commit c5b94c3, and the rule lives in storypole-cli handlers/remint/rules.rs.
